viral_posts.title_en:
i killed the infographics show with 1 claude opus prompt

now i made a full 10 minute story video in full code

this cost me $0 in ai video generations btw

turned it into a prompt you can use for free and make any topic u want, enjoy ↓

<inputs>
Ask me for my topic and my script. If I have no script, write one from my topic.
Ask which image model I have: GPT Image 2, or any model that takes reference images at 2K-4K, at about $0.03-0.05 an image.
Ask which voice I have: ElevenLabs, or Kokoro for free.
Before generating everything, show me a look test: one plate, one character sheet cut out and rigged, and a 10 s shot with typing, a tag and a character who talks and points. Wait for my OK.
</inputs>

<look>
A 1920x1080 animated explainer in the style of the big flat-vector infographic channels.
- Every line of narration is acted out by cartoon people inside a full illustrated place.
- All motion is code. There are no AI video generations, just a few still images that code cuts up, rigs and animates.

Art:
- Flat colour shapes with NO outlines, at most one slightly darker flat shade for form, simple geometric shapes and crisp edges.
- Muted palette: dusty blue-grey, slate teal, warm beige, navy, soft purple. Salmon-pink skin, big round heads, dot eyes, small bodies.
- Mood comes from the plate's own light: daylight, a cold blue night, warm indoor lamps.

Code colours:
- ink #2b2d42, red #d62828, orange #f4a261, gold #f6b93b, green #2fb37a, navy #1f2a48
- headline tomato #e2552f and purple #5b3fa6
- grey labels #8a8c9c, white cards #ffffff
- Font: Montserrat 800-900 (Google Fonts), all caps on cards and signs.

Pace:
- A new place every 3-4 s, about 10 places a minute.
- Something new arrives every 2 s: a tag, a stamp, a person walking in, a number.
- Never hold a still over 1 s. Never have a character who doesn't move.

Banned:
- outlines, glossy UI panels floating over the art, emoji, burned-in subtitles
- any channel's logo or name, photos of real people
- facts written on a plain colour card when the place could hold them
</look>

<art>
About 60 images in all ($2-3).

Every prompt starts with this style core, word for word:
"Flat vector illustration in exactly the same art style as the reference images: NO outlines or line art anywhere, every shape is a flat solid colour fill with at most one slightly darker flat shade for form, simple geometric shapes, crisp clean edges, no gradients, no texture, no painterly lighting. Muted modern palette: dusty blue-grey, slate teal, warm beige, navy, soft purple, salmon-pink skin. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos."

Then add one line that locks the setting ("The setting is [time, place]: [materials, light sources], nothing from other eras unless asked"). Feed 3-5 frames of a reference channel in as style references, with their logo cropped off.

1. Hero plates, about 24, one full 16:9 image each, for places you zoom into or come back to.
   - EMPTY: "no people, no characters, no animals".
   - Straight-on, with an open floor in the middle where characters will stand.
   - Blank signs, boards, screens and pages that code writes on later.
2. Quad plates, about 19, giving 76 more places. Pack 4 places into one image:
   "The image is a 2x2 grid of FOUR completely separate scenes, each filling exactly one quarter of the image (each quarter is itself a 16:9 picture), divided by perfectly straight thin pure-white gutters, one vertical down the exact centre and one horizontal across the exact centre."
   - Then describe the TOP-LEFT, TOP-RIGHT, BOTTOM-LEFT and BOTTOM-RIGHT scenes.
   - Split each quad on the brightest white row and column near the centre, walk out while the line stays over 60% white, and trim 6 px more.
   - Crop each tile to 16:9 at 1920x1080.
   - Object close-ups make great tiles: a desk, a screen, a document, a plate of food, a vault.
3. Main characters, 2-3 of them. Write one fixed description per character (age, hair, face, every piece of clothing with colours) and paste it word for word into every sheet.
   - Base sheet: 6 views. (1) front, neutral, drawn WITHOUT ARMS, only round smooth shoulder sockets where the arms would join; (2) the same armless front with a second emotion; (3) side view walking right; (4) seen from behind; (5) and (6) two poses the script needs.
   - Expression sheet: 6 armless fronts (hopeful, disgusted, terrified, exhausted, sick, shocked, or whatever the script needs), with the base sheet as a reference.
   - Pose sheet: 6 full poses with their props (sitting at a desk typing, sleeping, eating, running, signing, falling), with the base sheet as a reference.
4. Everyone else: role sheets of 4-6 people, each drawn in the exact pose their shot needs; crowd sheets of 8-10 small figures; prop sheets.
   - Every sheet: "on a solid flat chroma green background (#00B140) with lots of empty green space between figures; nothing touches, nothing on any character or object is green, full bodies, nothing cut off by the edges".
5. Thumbnail art: the same characters with richer saturated cartoon lighting and extreme emotions, the top quarter left free, no text, with the base sheets as references.
</art>

<rig>
Cutouts:
- The background is every border-connected pixel with G - max(R,B) over 40 and within 110 of the median green. Key only from the border, or dark clothes leak.
- Add a 2 px soft alpha band and clamp G to max(R,B) + 6 inside it, which kills the green fringe.
- Group the pieces by figure and drop specks. Name every sprite, and show me a named contact sheet.

Armless front figures become puppets:
- Split the head at the neck: the narrowest alpha row under the head.
- Find both shoulder sockets and the eye boxes.
- Inpaint the hole under the head from the body's own colours, so a nod never shows a gap.
- Write everything to rig.js: size, neck, sockets, eye boxes, skin RGB, sleeve RGB.
- Arms: upper L1 about 0.13 of the figure's height, lower L2 about 0.12, thickness about 0.04. Use sleeve colour to the elbow and skin for the forearm, a 0.82x darker sleeve when the arm is behind the body, and round caps and joins.
- Hands: mittens in three shapes (mitt, open, fist), plus a point with one finger out.
- Arm poses: each is a hand target relative to its shoulder, in units of L = L1 + L2, solved by two-bone IK (where there are two signs, the first is the left arm).
  - down: (∓0.04, 0.97)
  - rest: (±0.1, 0.9)
  - hips: (∓0.42, 0.55) with fists
  - point: right hand to (0.86, -0.32)
  - present: right hand to (0.75, 0.25), open
  - shrug: (∓0.62, 0.12), open
  - up: (∓0.32, -0.9)
  - hands on head
  - chin: a fist at the neck
  - hold: (±0.42, 0.45)
  - wave: (0.5, -0.75)
  - stop: (0.55, -0.1)
  - cheer: (∓0.55, -0.75) with fists
  - A pose change blends the two targets over 0.3-0.5 s with ease-in-out.
- Side, back and pose sprites stay whole images. Only the head turns, and a drawing or typing hand jitters ±6 px.
</rig>

<animation>
One HTML canvas where every frame is a pure function of time t: window .seek(t), READY, END, and EV, a list of sound events by name.
- Hang every shot on the narration: S('exact words', fn) starts a shot 0.08 s before that phrase. Repeated words are looked up by occurrence number.
- One function per shot, one shots file per chapter.

Motion primitives (Δ = t - start):
- pop: 0.3 s back-ease overshoot, 1 + 2.9(p-1)^3 + 1.9(p-1)^2.
- spring in: 1 - e^(-6.5Δ) cos(13Δ).
- kick on impact: 1 + 0.1 e^(-10Δ) cos(22Δ).
- shake: x = A e^(-8Δ) sin(61Δ), y = A e^(-8Δ) cos(47Δ).
- Exits shrink with ease-in over 0.25 s. Things arrive with a spring, a squash or a white puff, never a plain fade.

Camera:
- camP(plate, zoom, fx, fy) keeps the view inside the plate's edges.
- Every shot moves from one [zoom, fx, fy] to another with ease-in-out, a 2-4% push or a slow pan, so nothing holds still.
- Draw the plate and everything on it inside the same camera transform.
- Keep zoom under 1.33x on quad tiles. Zoom deeper only on hero plates.

Transitions:
- Push: the old shot slides out left while the new one slides in from the right, 0.24 s ease-in-out, with a whoosh 0.02 s before.
- Chapter splat: a #f4f1fb blob covers the screen in 0.2 s and clears in 0.2 s. It's a 1,250 px circle, 12 big satellite blobs at golden-angle spacing and 10 small droplets further out, shifted 120 px left on the way in and 140 px right on the way out.

Characters, alive in every frame:
- Breathing: scale 1 + 0.009 sin(2.3t).
- Head nod: 0.025 sin(2.1t) rad, or 0.025 sin(7t) + 0.02 sin(11.3t) while that character's line is spoken.
- Blink: every 2.7-4.2 s, seeded per figure. For 0.14 s, paint each eye box over in skin colour with a curved lash line.
- Walk:
  - Bob |sin| at 2.2% of the figure's height, with a body rock of ±0.035 rad.
  - Side-view walk sprites slide 1.5 leg lengths per step cycle, so the feet don't skate.
- Enter on the spring, sometimes with a hop. Fear is a fast shake (sin 70t). Surprise is a jump and an orange "!".
- A soft contact shadow ellipse under every figure. Night shots darken them with brightness(1 - k), so they match the plate.
- Every character on screen acts on its line: points at the thing being named, presents it, shrugs, cheers, holds its head.
</animation>

<graphics>
Text only lives on things in the world, typed letter by letter: 28 letters a second (34 for short tags). Each letter starts 1.45x big and 0.7 em to the right and settles in 0.18 s with ease-out.

The full kit:
- Board: a white rounded board (radius 20) that drops 420 px on the spring and swings 0.25 rad into place, or stands on a wooden post and swings up from -1 rad.
  - Soft drop shadow (blur 22, y 8, 22%) and a faint darker strip along its bottom edge.
  - Lines typed 0.3 s apart.
- Date card: top left at (70, 70), white, 120 px tall, at least 330 px wide, radius 18. An orange calendar icon, a grey "DATE:" at 26 px, the date typed at 44 px weight 900. Pops in over 0.32 s.
- Place card: the same card with a red map pin and "PLACE:".
- Tag: a 6 px line with a dot at the thing, drawn in 0.2 s, then a rounded pill (the text at 40 px weight 900) pops on its end. Ink, red, gold or orange pills.
- Number card: a white card with a small grey label and a big red number. Long numbers roll up like a counter with ease-out.
- Red X: two round 30 px strokes, 0.11 s each, 0.01 s apart, with a soft shadow. One goes over every wrong idea.
- Stamp: red text in a double rounded border, tilted -0.12 rad. It slams from 2.1x to 1x in 0.14 s, then kicks.
- Banner: a full-width headline band, 92 px white caps on tomato or purple, rotated -0.02 rad, sliding in from the left over 0.22 s.
- Speech bubble: white, radius 36, with a tail. Thought cloud: a pill with two small circles.
- Orange "?" that bobs and sways over a puzzled head, and an orange "!" pop.
- White puff and poof clouds, speed lines, light blue sweat drops, coins and bills, a soft vignette, and a colour tint for mood.
- Write on the plate's own blank boards, screens and pages whenever the place has them. Measure the blank's rectangle on a grid overlay of the plate first.
</graphics>

<voice>
- ElevenLabs: a deep, warm US documentary narrator, eleven_v4, stability 0.5, similarity 0.75, style 0, speaker boost, with the timestamps endpoint.
- About 170-180 words a minute, using the voice's own speed setting (1.0-1.1). Never speed it up with atempo: it sounds chipmunked.
- Long scripts go in 3 chunks split at chapter breaks, passing the previous and next text so the read stays continuous.
- Cut pauses over 0.24 s to 0.16 s, leave 0.5 s at chapter breaks, and add a 0.3 s lead-in.
- Rebuild word times from the alignment into words.js.
- Run faster-whisper over the result and diff it against the script before building the picture.
- Free route: Kokoro, then faster-whisper for the word times.
</voice>

<sound>
- Music: 2-3 free documentary beds from Pixabay, crossfaded over 3 s at big beats.
- Duck the music under the voice (30 ms attack, 0.3 s hold, 0.45 s release) and let it swell back up between chapters.
- SFX from Mixkit, one per event, aligned by their peaks, 6 dB quieter on speech: a typewriter tick on typing, a whoosh on pushes and splats, a pop on tags and cards, a thud on stamps, a hit on every red X, a ding on ticks, plus sounds that fit the scene.
- Gate: during speech the voice sits 15+ dB over music plus SFX (median of 100 ms frames), and the background is louder than the voice in under 1% of frames.
- Two-pass loudnorm to -14 LUFS, true peak -1 dB.
</sound>

<build>
1. Tools: Python, Playwright with Chromium or Edge, FFmpeg, faster-whisper, OpenCV, Pillow, numpy. Install what's missing and tell me what you installed.
2. Order:
   - the look test
   - the art in batches, with a contact sheet after each
   - cutouts and rig
   - voice and word times
   - shots, chapter by chapter
3. Check before any full render: a contact sheet per chapter, one frame every 2 s. Fix:
   - empty or overflowing signs
   - text over a face
   - black plate edges
   - feet floating off the floor
   - two shots in a row in the same place
   - any 4 s where nothing new arrives
4. Render at 30 fps, 4 motion-blur subframes over half a frame, frames piped to libx264 CRF 16-18.
   - Split long videos across 4-6 parallel browser pages and join the parts.
   - Scan the result for single-frame jumps and check that each one is a planned cut.
</build>

<gotchas>
- Too few places reads as lazy. One plate held for 30 s with cards over it looks cheap. Budget about 10 new places a minute.
- Some image models ignore "no arms". GPT Image 2 follows it.
- Paste the same character description into every sheet and feed the base sheet back in, or faces and clothes drift.
- Quad tiles are only about 1920 px wide. Pushing past 1.33x looks soft.
- Plates with people already drawn in can't be animated. Ask for EMPTY and check before cutting.
- Text on a card floating over the art looks like a slideshow. Write on the world.
- Long renders crash. Render in parts you can rerun, and back up the shot files before every big patch.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for my topic, my script, my image model and my voice, then make the look test.
</start>

- A soft contact shadow ellipse under every figure. Night shots darken them with brightness(1 - k), so they match the plate.
- Every character on screen acts on its line: points at the thing being named, presents it, shrugs, cheers, holds its head.
</animation>

<graphics>
Text only lives on things in the world, typed letter by letter: 28 letters a second (34 for short tags). Each letter starts 1.45x big and 0.7 em to the right and settles in 0.18 s with ease-out.

The full kit:
- Board: a white rounded board (radius 20) that drops 420 px on the spring and swings 0.25 rad into place, or stands on a wooden post and swings up from -1 rad.
  - Soft drop shadow (blur 22, y 8, 22%) and a faint darker strip along its bottom edge.
  - Lines typed 0.3 s apart.
- Date card: top left at (70, 70), white, 120 px tall, at least 330 px wide, radius 18. An orange calendar icon, a grey "DATE:" at 26 px, the date typed at 44 px weight 900. Pops in over 0.32 s.
- Place card: the same card with a red map pin and "PLACE:".
- Tag: a 6 px line with a dot at the thing, drawn in 0.2 s, then a rounded pill (the text at 40 px weight 900) pops on its end. Ink, red, gold or orange pills.
- Number card: a white card with a small grey label and a big red number. Long numbers roll up like a counter with ease-out.
- Red X: two round 30 px strokes, 0.11 s each, 0.01 s apart, with a soft shadow. One goes over every wrong idea.
- Stamp: red text in a double rounded border, tilted -0.12 rad. It slams from 2.1x to 1x in 0.14 s, then kicks.
- Banner: a full-width headline band, 92 px white caps on tomato or purple, rotated -0.02 rad, sliding in from the left over 0.22 s.
- Speech bubble: white, radius 36, with a tail. Thought cloud: a pill with two small circles.
- Orange "?" that bobs and sways over a puzzled head, and an orange "!" pop.
- White puff and poof clouds, speed lines, light blue sweat drops, coins and bills, a soft vignette, and a colour tint for mood.
- Write on the plate's own blank boards, screens and pages whenever the place has them. Measure the blank's rectangle on a grid overlay of the plate first.
</graphics>

<voice>
- ElevenLabs: a deep, warm US documentary narrator, eleven_v4, stability 0.5, similarity 0.75, style 0, speaker boost, with the timestamps endpoint.
- About 170-180 words a minute, using the voice's own speed setting (1.0-1.1). Never speed it up with atempo: it sounds chipmunked.
- Long scripts go in 3 chunks split at chapter breaks, passing the previous and next text so the read stays continuous.
- Cut pauses over 0.24 s to 0.16 s, leave 0.5 s at chapter breaks, and add a 0.3 s lead-in.
- Rebuild word times from the alignment into words.js.
- Run faster-whisper over the result and diff it against the script before building the picture.
- Free route: Kokoro, then faster-whisper for the word times.
</voice>

<sound>
- Music: 2-3 free documentary beds from Pixabay, crossfaded over 3 s at big beats.
- Duck the music under the voice (30 ms attack, 0.3 s hold, 0.45 s release) and let it swell back up between chapters.
- SFX from Mixkit, one per event, aligned by their peaks, 6 dB quieter on speech: a typewriter tick on typing, a whoosh on pushes and splats, a pop on tags and cards, a thud on stamps, a hit on every red X, a ding on ticks, plus sounds that fit the scene.
- Gate: during speech the voice sits 15+ dB over music plus SFX (median of 100 ms frames), and the background is louder than the voice in under 1% of frames.
- Two-pass loudnorm to -14 LUFS, true peak -1 dB.
</sound>

<build>
1. Tools: Python, Playwright with Chromium or Edge, FFmpeg, faster-whisper, OpenCV, Pillow, numpy. Install what's missing and tell me what you installed.
2. Order:
   - the look test
   - the art in batches, with a contact sheet after each
   - cutouts and rig
   - voice and word times
   - shots, chapter by chapter
3. Check before any full render: a contact sheet per chapter, one frame every 2 s. Fix:
   - empty or overflowing signs
   - text over a face
   - black plate edges
   - feet floating off the floor
   - two shots in a row in the same place
   - any 4 s where nothing new arrives
4. Render at 30 fps, 4 motion-blur subframes over half a frame, frames piped to libx264 CRF 16-18.
   - Split long videos across 4-6 parallel browser pages and join the parts.
   - Scan the result for single-frame jumps and check that each one is a planned cut.
</build>

<gotchas>
- Too few places reads as lazy. One plate held for 30 s with cards over it looks cheap. Budget about 10 new places a minute.
- Some image models ignore "no arms". GPT Image 2 follows it.
- Paste the same character description into every sheet and feed the base sheet back in, or faces and clothes drift.
- Quad tiles are only about 1920 px wide. Pushing past 1.33x looks soft.
- Plates with people already drawn in can't be animated. Ask for EMPTY and check before cutting.
- Text on a card floating over the art looks like a slideshow. Write on the world.
- Long renders crash. Render in parts you can rerun, and back up the shot files before every big patch.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for my topic, my script, my image model and my voice, then make the look test.
</start>

我用 1 个克劳德作品提示杀死了信息图表节目

现在我用完整代码制作了一个完整的 10 分钟故事视频

顺便说一句，这花了我 0 美元的人工智能视频生成

把它变成了一个提示，你可以免费使用并制作任何你想要的主题，享受吧↓

<输入>
向我询问我的主题和剧本。如果我没有脚本，请根据我的主题写一个。
询问我有哪种图像模型：GPT Image 2，或任何以 2K-4K 拍摄参考图像的模型，每张图像的价格约为 0.03-0.05 美元。
询问我有哪种声音：ElevenLabs，或免费的 Kokoro。
在生成所有内容之前，先给我看一下外观测试：一个盘子、一个被剪下来并装配好的角色表，以及一个 10 秒的打字镜头、一个标签和一个会说话和指点的角色。等我好了。
</输入>

<看>
大型平面矢量信息图表频道风格的 1920x1080 动画讲解器。
- 每一行叙述都由卡通人物在一个充满插图的地方表演。
- 所有的动作都是代码。没有人工智能视频生成，只有一些经过代码切割、装配和动画处理的静态图像。

艺术：
- 没有轮廓的扁平颜色形状，最多一种稍暗的扁平色调，简单的几何形状和清晰的边缘。
- 柔和的调色板：灰蓝灰色、板岩青色、暖米色、海军蓝、柔和的紫色。鲑鱼粉色的皮肤，圆圆的大脑袋，圆点的眼睛，小小的身体。
- 情绪来自于盘子本身的光线：日光、寒冷的蓝色夜晚、温暖的室内灯光。

代码颜色：
- 墨水 #2b2d42、红色 #d62828、橙色 #f4a261、金色 #f6b93b、绿色 #2fb37a、海军蓝 #1f2a48
- 标题番茄#e2552f 和紫色#5b3fa6
- 灰色标签#8a8c9c，白色卡片#ffffff
- 字体：Montserrat 800-900（Google 字体），卡片和标志上全部大写。

步速：
- 每 3-4 秒一个新位置，每分钟大约 10 个位置。
- 每 2 秒就会有新的东西到达：标签、邮票、走进来的人、号码。
- 切勿保持静止超过 1 秒。永远不要有不动的角色。

禁止：
- 轮廓、漂浮在艺术上方的光滑 UI 面板、表情符号、内置字幕
- 任何频道的标志或名称、真人照片
- 当地方可以容纳时，将事实写在普通彩色卡片上
</看>

<艺术>
总共大约 60 张图片（2-3 美元）。

每个提示都以这种风格核心开头，逐字逐句：
“平面矢量插图的艺术风格与参考图像完全相同：任何地方都没有轮廓或线条艺术，每个形状都是平面纯色填充，最多有一个稍暗的平面阴影作为形式，简单的几何形状，清晰干净的边缘，没有渐变，没有纹理，没有绘画照明。柔和的现代调色板：灰蓝色，板岩青色，温暖米色，海军蓝，柔和的紫色，鲑鱼粉红色皮肤。没有文字，没有字母，没有数字，没有徽标。”

然后添加一行来锁定设置（“设置是[时间，地点]：[材料，光源]，除非询问，否则没有其他时代的内容”）。将参考通道的 3-5 帧作为样式参考，并剪掉其徽标。

1. 英雄板块，大约 24 张，每张一张完整的 16:9 图片，用于您放大或返回的地方。
- 空：“没有人，没有人物，没有动物”。
- 直行，中间有一个开放的地板，角色可以站立。
- 稍后在上面写入代码的空白标志、板、屏幕和页面。
2.四块板，大约19个，多出76个位置。将 4 个位置打包到一张图像中：
“该图像是由四个完全独立的场景组成的 2x2 网格，每个场景正好填充图像的四分之一（每个四分之一本身就是一张 16:9 的图片），由完全笔直的纯白色排水沟划分，一个垂直向下，一个水平穿过正中心。”
- 然后描述左上、右上、左下和右下场景。
- 在中心附近最亮的白色行和列上分割每个四边形，在线条保持超过 60% 的白色时走出去，然后再修剪 6 像素。
- 在 1920x1080 下将每个图块裁剪为 16:9。
- 物体特写可以成为很棒的图块：一张桌子、一个屏幕、一份文件、一盘食物、一个金库。
3.主要人物，2-3人。为每个角色写一个固定的描述（年龄、头发、脸、每件衣服的颜色），然后逐字粘贴到每张纸上。
- 基础表：6 次查看。 (1) 正面，中立，没有手臂，只有手臂连接处的圆形光滑肩窝； （2）同样无臂的正面却有第二种情感； (3)右侧行走侧视图； (4) 从后面看； (5)和(6)两个构成脚本需要。
- 表情表：6 个无臂正面（希望、厌恶、恐惧、疲惫、生病、震惊或脚本需要的任何内容），以基础表作为参考。
- 姿势表：6 个带有道具的完整姿势（坐在办公桌前打字、睡觉、吃饭、跑步、签名、摔倒），以基础表作为参考。
4. 其他人：4-6 人的角色表，每个人都按照他们的拍摄需要的准确姿势绘制； 8-10 个小数字的人群表；道具表。
- 每张纸：“在坚实的平坦色度绿色背景上（#00B140），人物之间有很多空白的绿色空间；没有任何接触，任何角色或物体上没有任何东西是绿色的，全身，没有被边缘切断的东西”。
5.缩略图艺术：相同的角色，具有更丰富的饱和卡通灯光和极端的情感，上四分之一留空，没有文字，以底纸为参考。
</艺术>

<装备>
剪纸：
- 背景是 G - max(R,B) 超过 40 且在中值绿色 110 以内的每个边界连接像素。钥匙只能从边框处，否则深色衣服会漏。
- 添加 2 px 软 alpha 带并将 G 钳位到其中的 max(R,B) + 6，这会消除绿色边缘。
- 按图形和掉落斑点对碎片进行分组。给每个精灵命名，然后给我看一张命名的联系表。

无臂的正面人物变成了木偶：
- 将头部在颈部分开：头部下方最窄的 alpha 行。
- 找到肩窝和眼窝。
- 用身体本身的颜色修补头下的洞，这样点头就不会出现间隙。
- 将所有内容写入 rig.js：尺寸、颈部、插座、眼框、皮肤 RGB、袖子 RGB。
- 手臂：上L1约为人物高度的0.13，下L2约为0.12，厚度约为0.04。对肘部和前臂皮肤使用袖子颜色，当手臂位于身体后方时，使用 0.82 倍深的袖子，以及圆形帽和连接处。
- 手：三种形状的连指手套（手套、张开、拳头），加上一根手指伸出的点。
- 手臂姿势：每个都是相对于肩膀的手部目标，单位为L = L1 + L2，通过二骨IK解决（其中有两个标志，第一个是左臂）。
- 向下：(∓0.04, 0.97)
- 休息：（±0.1，0.9）
- 臀部：(∓0.42, 0.55) 用拳头
- 点：右手到（0.86，-0.32）
- 现在：右手到（0.75，0.25），打开
- 耸肩：(∓0.62, 0.12)，打开
- 向上：(∓0.32，-0.9)
- 双手放在头上
- 下巴：拳头放在脖子上
- 保持：（±0.42，0.45）
- 波：（0.5，-0.75）
- 停止：(0.55，-0.1)
- 欢呼：（∓0.55，-0.75）用拳头
- 姿势变化在 0.3-0.5 秒内通过缓入缓出混合两个目标。
- 侧面、背面和姿势精灵保持完整图像。只有头部转动，绘图或打字的手抖动±6 px。
</钻>

<动画>
一个 HTML 画布，其中每一帧都是时间 t 的纯函数：window .seek(t)、READY、END 和 EV，按名称列出的声音事件列表。
- 将每个镜头挂在旁白上：S('exact Words', fn) 在该短语之前 0.08 秒开始一个镜头。重复的单词按出现次数查找。
- 每个镜头一个功能，每个章节一个镜头文件。

运动基元（Δ = t - 开始）：
- 弹出：0.3 秒后缓超调，1 + 2.9(p-1)^3 + 1.9(p-1)^2。
- 弹簧输入：1 - e^(-6.5Δ) cos(13Δ)。
- 冲击力踢：1 + 0.1 e^(-10Δ) cos(22Δ)。
- 摇动：x = A e^(-8Δ) sin(61Δ)，y = A e^(-8Δ) cos(47Δ)。
- 退出时间随着缓入时间的延长而缩小，时间超过 0.25 秒。事物到来时会伴随着春天、南瓜或白色的泡芙，而不是简单的褪色。

相机：
- camP（plate，zoom，fx，fy）将视图保持在板边缘内。
- 每个镜头都会通过缓入、2-4% 的推力或缓慢的平移从一个 [zoom、fx、fy] 移动到另一个，因此没有什么是静止的。
- 在同一相机变换内绘制盘子及其上的所有内容。
- 将四块图块上的缩放保持在 1.33 倍以下。仅在英雄板块上进行更深入的缩放。

过渡：
- 推：旧镜头从左侧滑出，新镜头从右侧滑入，0.24 秒缓入，之前有 0.02 秒的嗖嗖声。
- 章节 splat：#f4f1fb 斑点在 0.2 秒内覆盖屏幕并在 0.2 秒内清除。它是一个 1,250 像素的圆圈，由 12 个黄金角间距的大卫星斑点和更远的 10 个小水滴组成，在进入时向左移动 120 像素，在离开时向右移动 140 像素。

每一帧都充满活力的人物：
- 呼吸：标度 1 + 0.009 sin(2.3t)。
- 点头：0.025 sin(2.1t) rad，或 0.025 sin(7t) + 0.02 sin(11.3t)，同时说出该角色的台词。
- 闪烁：每 2.7-4.2 秒，每个数字播种。在 0.14 秒内，用弯曲的睫毛线将每个眼框涂上肤色。
- 步行：
- 鲍勃|罪|位于人物高度的 2.2% 处，主体岩石为 ±0.035 rad。
- 侧视行走精灵每个步循环滑动 1.5 条腿长，因此脚不会滑行。
- 进入泉水，有时会跳跃。恐惧是一种快速的震动（sin 70t）。惊喜是一个跳跃和一个橙色的“！”。
- 每个人物下方都有一个柔和的接触阴影椭圆。夜间拍摄的照片会用亮度 (1 - k) 使它们变暗，因此它们与车牌相匹配。
- 屏幕上的每个角色都按照自己的路线行事：指向被命名的事物，展示它，耸肩，欢呼，抬起头。
</动画>

<图形>
文本只存在于世界上的事物上，逐个字母地输入：每秒 28 个字母（短标签为 34 个）。每个字母以 1.45 倍大和向右 0.7 倍高度开始，并在 0.18 秒内稳定下来并缓出。

完整套件：
- 板：白色圆形板（半径 20），在弹簧上下降 420 px，摆动 0.25 rad 到位，或者站在木柱上，从 -1 rad 向上摆动。
- 柔和的阴影（模糊 22、y 8、22%）和沿其底部边缘的微弱深色条带。
- 输入的行之间间隔 0.3 秒。
- 日期卡：左上角 (70, 70)，白色，高 120 像素，宽至少 330 像素，半径 18。橙色日历图标，26 像素处有灰色“日期：”，以 44 像素粗细 900 输入日期。弹出时间超过 0.32 秒。
- 地点卡：带有红色地图图钉和“地点：”的同一张卡。
- 标签：一条 6 px 线，在物体上有一个点，在 0.2 秒内绘制，然后在其末端弹出一个圆形药丸（40 px 粗细 900 的文本）。墨水、红色、金色或橙色药丸。
- 号码卡：一张白色卡片，上面有一个灰色的小标签和一个红色的大数字。长数字像带有缓出功能的计数器一样滚动。
- 红色 X：两个圆形 30 px 笔划，每个 0.11 秒，间隔 0.01 秒，带有柔和的阴影。人们要仔细检查每一个错误的想法。
- 印章：双圆边框中的红色文本，倾斜 -0.12 rad。它在 0.14 秒内从 2.1 倍猛烈撞击到 1 倍，然后踢动。
- 横幅：全宽标题带，92 像素白色番茄或紫色帽子，旋转 -0.02 rad，从左侧滑入 0.22 秒。
- 语音气泡：白色，半径36，有尾巴。思想云：一颗有两个小圆圈的药丸。
- 橙子 ”？”它在一个困惑的头上晃动和摇摆，还有一个橙色的“！”流行音乐。
- 白色的云彩、速度线、浅蓝色的汗滴、硬币和钞票、柔和的小插图以及适合心情的色调。
- 只要该地方有空白板、屏幕和页面，就可以在该板块自己的空白板、屏幕和页面上书写。首先在板的网格覆盖层上测量毛坯的矩形。
</图形>

<声音>
- ElevenLabs：深度、温暖的美国纪录片旁白，eleven_v4，稳定性0.5，相似度0.75，风格0，扬声器增强，带有时间戳端点。
- 大约每分钟 170-180 个单词，使用语音自身的速度设置 (1.0-1.1)。永远不要用 Atempo 加快速度：听起来很花哨。
- 长脚本分为 3 个块，在章节中断处分割，传递上一个和下一个文本，以便阅读保持连续。
- 将 0.24 秒以上的停顿削减至 0.16 秒，在章节休息处留出 0.5 秒，并添加 0.3 秒的导入时间。
- 将对齐方式重建单词时间到words.js。
- 运行速度更快，在构建图片之前仔细研究结果并将其与脚本进行比较。
- 免费路线：Kokoro，然后更快地耳语单词时间。
</语音>

<声音>
- 音乐：Pixabay 上的 2-3 张免费纪录片床，以大节奏交叉淡入淡出超过 3 秒。
- 将音乐隐藏在声音下方（30 毫秒起音，0.3 秒保持，0.45 秒释放）并让它在章节之间回升。
- 来自 Mixkit 的 SFX，每个事件一个，按峰值对齐，语音时安静 6 dB：打字时的打字声、推动和敲击时的呼啸声、标签和卡片上的流行声、邮票上的重击声、每个红色 X 上的敲击声、滴答声上的叮当声，以及适合场景的声音。
- 门限：在演讲期间，声音比音乐加 SFX（100 毫秒帧的中值）高 15+ dB，并且背景比帧中的声音大 1%。
- 两次通过响度至 -14 LUFS，真实峰值 -1 dB。
</声音>

viral_posts.summary_zh:
询问我的主题和剧本。如果我没有脚本，请根据我的主题写一个。
询问我有哪种图像模型：GPT Image 2，或任何以 2K-4K 拍摄参考图像的模型，每张图像的价格约为 0.03-0.05 美元。

<看>
大型平面矢量信息图表频道风格的 1920x1080 动画讲解器。
- 每一行叙述都由卡通人物在一个充满插图的地方表演。
- 所有的动作都是代码。没有人工智能视频生成，只有一些经过代码切割、装配和动画处理的静态图像。

艺术：
- 没有轮廓的扁平颜色形状，最多一种稍暗的扁平色调，简单的几何形状和清晰的边缘。
- 柔和的调色板：灰蓝灰色、板岩青色、暖米色、海军蓝、柔和的紫色。鲑鱼粉色的皮肤，圆圆的大脑袋，圆点的眼睛，小小的身体。
- 情绪来自于盘子本身的光线：日光、寒冷的蓝色夜晚、温暖的室内灯光。

代码颜色：
- 墨水 #2b2d42、红色 #d62828、橙色 #f4a261、金色 #f6b93b、绿色 #2fb37a、海军蓝 #1f2a48
- 标题番茄#e2552f 和紫色#5b3fa6
- 灰色标签#8a8c9c，白色卡片#ffffff
- 字体：Montserrat 800-900（Google 字体），卡片和标志上全部大写。

步速：
- 每 3-4 秒一个新位置，每分钟大约 10 个位置。
- 每 2 秒就会有新的东西到达：标签、邮票、走进来的人、号码。
- 切勿保持静止超过 1 秒。永远不要有不动的角色。

禁止：
- 轮廓、漂浮在艺术上方的光滑 UI 面板、表情符号、内置字幕
- 任何频道的标志或名称、真人照片
- 当地方可以容纳时，将事实写在普通彩色卡片上
</看>

<艺术>
总共大约 60 张图片（2-3 美元）。

每个提示都以这种风格核心开头，逐字逐句：
“平面矢量插图的艺术风格与参考图像完全相同：任何地方都没有轮廓或线条艺术，每个形状都是平面纯色填充，最多有一个稍暗的平面阴影作为形式，简单的几何形状，清晰干净的边缘，没有渐变，没有纹理，没有绘画照明。柔和的现代调色板：灰蓝色，板岩青色，温暖米色，海军蓝，柔和的紫色，鲑鱼粉红色皮肤。没有文字，没有字母，没有数字，没有徽标。”

然后添加一行来锁定设置（“设置是[时间，地点]：[材料，光源]，除非询问，否则没有其他时代的内容”）。将参考通道的 3-5 帧作为样式参考，并剪掉其徽标。

1. 英雄板块，大约 24 张，每张一张完整的 16:9 图片，用于您放大或返回的地方。
- 空：“没有人，没有人物，没有动物”。
- 直行，中间有一个开放的地板，角色可以站立。
- 稍后在上面写入代码的空白标志、板、屏幕和页面。
2.四块板，大约19个，多出76个位置。将 4 个位置打包到一张图像中：
“该图像是由四个完全独立的场景组成的 2x2 网格，每个场景正好填充图像的四分之一（每个四分之一本身就是一张 16:9 的图片），由完全笔直的纯白色排水沟划分，一个垂直向下，一个水平穿过正中心。”
- 然后描述左上、右上、左下和右下场景。
- 在中心附近最亮的白色行和列上分割每个四边形，在线条保持超过 60% 的白色时走出去，然后再修剪 6 像素。
- 在 1920x1080 下将每个图块裁剪为 16:9。

5.缩略图艺术：相同的角色，具有更丰富的饱和卡通灯光和极端的情感，上四分之一留空，没有文字，以底纸为参考。

<装备>
剪纸：
- 背景是 G - max(R,B) 超过 40 且在中值绿色 110 以内的每个边界连接像素。钥匙只能从边框处，否则深色衣服会漏。

- 按图形和掉落斑点对碎片进行分组。给每个精灵命名，然后给我看一张命名的联系表。

无臂的正面人物变成了木偶：
- 将头部在颈部分开：头部下方最窄的 alpha 行。
- 找到肩窝和眼窝。
- 用身体本身的颜色修补头下的洞，这样点头就不会出现间隙。
- 将所有内容写入 rig.js：尺寸、颈部、插座、眼框、皮肤 RGB、袖子 RGB。

- 手：三种形状的连指手套（手套、张开、拳头），加上一根手指伸出的点。
- 手臂姿势：每个都是相对于肩膀的手部目标，单位为L = L1 + L2，通过二骨IK解决（其中有两个标志，第一个是左臂）。
- 向下：(∓0.04, 0.97)
- 休息：（±0.1，0.9）
- 臀部：(∓0.42, 0.55) 用拳头
- 点：右手到（0.86，-0.32）
- 现在：右手到（0.75，0.25），打开
- 耸肩：(∓0.62, 0.12)，打开
- 向上：(∓0.32，-0.9)
- 双手放在头上
- 下巴：拳头放在脖子上
- 保持：（±0.42，0.45）
- 波：（0.5，-0.75）
- 停止：(0.55，-0.1)
- 欢呼：（∓0.55，-0.75）用拳头
- 姿势变化在 0.3-0.5 秒内通过缓入缓出混合两个目标。
- 侧面、背面和姿势精灵保持完整图像。只有头部转动，绘图或打字的手抖动±6 px。
</钻>

<动画>
一个 HTML 画布，其中每一帧都是时间 t 的纯函数：window .seek(t)、READY、END 和 EV，按名称列出的声音事件列表。
- 将每个镜头挂在旁白上：S('exact Words', fn) 在该短语之前 0.08 秒开始一个镜头。重复的单词按出现次数查找。
- 每个镜头一个功能，每个章节一个镜头文件。

运动基元（Δ = t - 开始）：
- 弹出：0.3 秒后缓超调，1 + 2.9(p-1)^3 + 1.9(p-1)^2。
- 弹簧输入：1 - e^(-6.5Δ) cos(13Δ)。
- 冲击力踢：1 + 0.1 e^(-10Δ) cos(22Δ)。
- 摇动：x = A e^(-8Δ) sin(61Δ)，y = A e^(-8Δ) cos(47Δ)。
- 退出时间随着缓入时间的延长而缩小，时间超过 0.25 秒。事物到来时会伴随着春天、南瓜或白色的泡芙，而不是简单的褪色。

- camP（plate，zoom，fx，fy）将视图保持在板边缘内。
- 每个镜头都会通过缓入、2-4% 的推力或缓慢的平移从一个 [zoom、fx、fy] 移动到另一个，因此没有什么是静止的。

- 每个人物下方都有一个柔和的接触阴影椭圆。夜间拍摄的照片会用亮度 (1 - k) 使它们变暗，因此它们与车牌相匹配。
- 屏幕上的每个角色都按照自己的路线行事：指向被命名的事物，展示它，耸肩，欢呼，抬起头。
</动画>

<图形>

- 橙子 ”？”它在一个困惑的头上晃动和摇摆，还有一个橙色的“！”流行音乐。

</图形>

viral_posts.summary_en:
i killed the infographics show with 1 claude opus prompt

now i made a full 10 minute story video in full code

this cost me $0 in ai video generations btw

turned it into a prompt you can use for free and make any topic u want, enjoy ↓

<inputs>
Ask me for my topic and my script. If I have no script, write one from my topic.
Ask which image model I have: GPT Image 2, or any model that takes reference images at 2K-4K, at about $0.03-0.05 an image.
Ask which voice I have: ElevenLabs, or Kokoro for free.
Before generating everything, show me a look test: one plate, one character sheet cut out and rigged, and a 10 s shot with typing, a tag and a character who talks and points. Wait for my OK.
</inputs>

<look>
A 1920x1080 animated explainer in the style of the big flat-vector infographic channels.
- Every line of narration is acted out by cartoon people inside a full illustrated place.
- All motion is code. There are no AI video generations, just a few still images that code cuts up, rigs and animates.

Art:
- Flat colour shapes with NO outlines, at most one slightly darker flat shade for form, simple geometric shapes and crisp edges.
- Muted palette: dusty blue-grey, slate teal, warm beige, navy, soft purple. Salmon-pink skin, big round heads, dot eyes, small bodies.
- Mood comes from the plate's own light: daylight, a cold blue night, warm indoor lamps.

Code colours:
- ink #2b2d42, red #d62828, orange #f4a261, gold #f6b93b, green #2fb37a, navy #1f2a48
- headline tomato #e2552f and purple #5b3fa6
- grey labels #8a8c9c, white cards #ffffff
- Font: Montserrat 800-900 (Google Fonts), all caps on cards and signs.

Pace:
- A new place every 3-4 s, about 10 places a minute.
- Something new arrives every 2 s: a tag, a stamp, a person walking in, a number.
- Never hold a still over 1 s. Never have a character who doesn't move.

Banned:
- outlines, glossy UI panels floating over the art, emoji, burned-in subtitles
- any channel's logo or name, photos of real people
- facts written on a plain colour card when the place could hold them
</look>

<art>
About 60 images in all ($2-3).

Every prompt starts with this style core, word for word:
"Flat vector illustration in exactly the same art style as the reference images: NO outlines or line art anywhere, every shape is a flat solid colour fill with at most one slightly darker flat shade for form, simple geometric shapes, crisp clean edges, no gradients, no texture, no painterly lighting. Muted modern palette: dusty blue-grey, slate teal, warm beige, navy, soft purple, salmon-pink skin. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos."

Then add one line that locks the setting ("The setting is [time, place]: [materials, light sources], nothing from other eras unless asked"). Feed 3-5 frames of a reference channel in as style references, with their logo cropped off.

1. Hero plates, about 24, one full 16:9 image each, for places you zoom into or come back to.
   - EMPTY: "no people, no characters, no animals".
   - Straight-on, with an open floor in the middle where characters will stand.
   - Blank signs, boards, screens and pages that code writes on later.
2. Quad plates, about 19, giving 76 more places. Pack 4 places into one image:
   "The image is a 2x2 grid of FOUR completely separate scenes, each filling exactly one quarter of the image (each quarter is itself a 16:9 picture), divided by perfectly straight thin pure-white gutters, one vertical down the exact centre and one horizontal across the exact centre."
   - Then describe the TOP-LEFT, TOP-RIGHT, BOTTOM-LEFT and BOTTOM-RIGHT scenes.
   - Split each quad on the brightest white row and column near the centre, walk out while the line stays over 60% white, and trim 6 px more.
   - Crop each tile to 16:9 at 1920x1080.
   - Object close-ups make great tiles: a desk, a screen, a document, a plate of food, a vault.
3. Main characters, 2-3 of them. Write one fixed description per character (age, hair, face, every piece of clothing with colours) and paste it word for word into every sheet.
   - Base sheet: 6 views. (1) front, neutral, drawn WITHOUT ARMS, only round smooth shoulder sockets where the arms would join; (2) the same armless front with a second emotion; (3) side view walking right; (4) seen from behind; (5) and (6) two poses the script needs.
   - Expression sheet: 6 armless fronts (hopeful, disgusted, terrified, exhausted, sick, shocked, or whatever the script needs), with the base sheet as a reference.
   - Pose sheet: 6 full poses with their props (sitting at a desk typing, sleeping, eating, running, signing, falling), with the base sheet as a reference.
4. Everyone else: role sheets of 4-6 people, each drawn in the exact pose their shot needs; crowd sheets of 8-10 small figures; prop sheets.
   - Every sheet: "on a solid flat chroma green background (#00B140) with lots of empty green space between figures; nothing touches, nothing on any character or object is green, full bodies, nothing cut off by the edges".
5. Thumbnail art: the same characters with richer saturated cartoon lighting and extreme emotions, the top quarter left free, no text, with the base sheets as references.
</art>

<rig>
Cutouts:
- The background is every border-connected pixel with G - max(R,B) over 40 and within 110 of the median green. Key only from the border, or dark clothes leak.
- Add a 2 px soft alpha band and clamp G to max(R,B) + 6 inside it, which kills the green fringe.
- Group the pieces by figure and drop specks. Name every sprite, and show me a named contact sheet.

Armless front figures become puppets:
- Split the head at the neck: the narrowest alpha row under the head.
- Find both shoulder sockets and the eye boxes.
- Inpaint the hole under the head from the body's own colours, so a nod never shows a gap.
- Write everything to rig.js: size, neck, sockets, eye boxes, skin RGB, sleeve RGB.
- Arms: upper L1 about 0.13 of the figure's height, lower L2 about 0.12, thickness about 0.04. Use sleeve colour to the elbow and skin for the forearm, a 0.82x darker sleeve when the arm is behind the body, and round caps and joins.
- Hands: mittens in three shapes (mitt, open, fist), plus a point with one finger out.
- Arm poses: each is a hand target relative to its shoulder, in units of L = L1 + L2, solved by two-bone IK (where there are two signs, the first is the left arm).
  - down: (∓0.04, 0.97)
  - rest: (±0.1, 0.9)
  - hips: (∓0.42, 0.55) with fists
  - point: right hand to (0.86, -0.32)
  - present: right hand to (0.75, 0.25), open
  - shrug: (∓0.62, 0.12), open
  - up: (∓0.32, -0.9)
  - hands on head
  - chin: a fist at the neck
  - hold: (±0.42, 0.45)
  - wave: (0.5, -0.75)
  - stop: (0.55, -0.1)
  - cheer: (∓0.55, -0.75) with fists
  - A pose change blends the two targets over 0.3-0.5 s with ease-in-out.
- Side, back and pose sprites stay whole images. Only the head turns, and a drawing or typing hand jitters ±6 px.
</rig>

<animation>
One HTML canvas where every frame is a pure function of time t: window .seek(t), READY, END, and EV, a list of sound events by name.
- Hang every shot on the narration: S('exact words', fn) starts a shot 0.08 s before that phrase. Repeated words are looked up by occurrence number.
- One function per shot, one shots file per chapter.

Motion primitives (Δ = t - start):
- pop: 0.3 s back-ease overshoot, 1 + 2.9(p-1)^3 + 1.9(p-1)^2.
- spring in: 1 - e^(-6.5Δ) cos(13Δ).
- kick on impact: 1 + 0.1 e^(-10Δ) cos(22Δ).
- shake: x = A e^(-8Δ) sin(61Δ), y = A e^(-8Δ) cos(47Δ).
- Exits shrink with ease-in over 0.25 s. Things arrive with a spring, a squash or a white puff, never a plain fade.

Camera:
- camP(plate, zoom, fx, fy) keeps the view inside the plate's edges.
- Every shot moves from one [zoom, fx, fy] to another with ease-in-out, a 2-4% push or a slow pan, so nothing holds still.
- Draw the plate and everything on it inside the same camera transform.
- Keep zoom under 1.33x on quad tiles. Zoom deeper only on hero plates.

Transitions:
- Push: the old shot slides out left while the new one slides in from the right, 0.24 s ease-in-out, with a whoosh 0.02 s before.
- Chapter splat: a #f4f1fb blob covers the screen in 0.2 s and clears in 0.2 s. It's a 1,250 px circle, 12 big satellite blobs at golden-angle spacing and 10 small droplets further out, shifted 120 px left on the way in and 140 px right on the way out.

Characters, alive in every frame:
- Breathing: scale 1 + 0.009 sin(2.3t).
- Head nod: 0.025 sin(2.1t) rad, or 0.025 sin(7t) + 0.02 sin(11.3t) while that character's line is spoken.
- Blink: every 2.7-4.2 s, seeded per figure. For 0.14 s, paint each eye box over in skin colour with a curved lash line.
- Walk:
  - Bob |sin| at 2.2% of the figure's height, with a body rock of ±0.035 rad.
  - Side-view walk sprites slide 1.5 leg lengths per step cycle, so the feet don't skate.
- Enter on the spring, sometimes with a hop. Fear is a fast shake (sin 70t). Surprise is a jump and an orange "!".
- A soft contact shadow ellipse under every figure. Night shots darken them with brightness(1 - k), so they match the plate.
- Every character on screen acts on its line: points at the thing being named, presents it, shrugs, cheers, holds its head.
</animation>

<graphics>
Text only lives on things in the world, typed letter by letter: 28 letters a second (34 for short tags). Each letter starts 1.45x big and 0.7 em to the right and settles in 0.18 s with ease-out.

The full kit:
- Board: a white rounded board (radius 20) that drops 420 px on the spring and swings 0.25 rad into place, or stands on a wooden post and swings up from -1 rad.
  - Soft drop shadow (blur 22, y 8, 22%) and a faint darker strip along its bottom edge.
  - Lines typed 0.3 s apart.
- Date card: top left at (70, 70), white, 120 px tall, at least 330 px wide, radius 18. An orange calendar icon, a grey "DATE:" at 26 px, the date typed at 44 px weight 900. Pops in over 0.32 s.
- Place card: the same card with a red map pin and "PLACE:".
- Tag: a 6 px line with a dot at the thing, drawn in 0.2 s, then a rounded pill (the text at 40 px weight 900) pops on its end. Ink, red, gold or orange pills.
- Number card: a white card with a small grey label and a big red number. Long numbers roll up like a counter with ease-out.
- Red X: two round 30 px strokes, 0.11 s each, 0.01 s apart, with a soft shadow. One goes over every wrong idea.
- Stamp: red text in a double rounded border, tilted -0.12 rad. It slams from 2.1x to 1x in 0.14 s, then kicks.
- Banner: a full-width headline band, 92 px white caps on tomato or purple, rotated -0.02 rad, sliding in from the left over 0.22 s.
- Speech bubble: white, radius 36, with a tail. Thought cloud: a pill with two small circles.
- Orange "?" that bobs and sways over a puzzled head, and an orange "!" pop.
- White puff and poof clouds, speed lines, light blue sweat drops, coins and bills, a soft vignette, and a colour tint for mood.
- Write on the plate's own blank boards, screens and pages whenever the place has them. Measure the blank's rectangle on a grid overlay of the plate first.
</graphics>

<voice>
- ElevenLabs: a deep, warm US documentary narrator, eleven_v4, stability 0.5, similarity 0.75, style 0, speaker boost, with the timestamps endpoint.
- About 170-180 words a minute, using the voice's own speed setting (1.0-1.1). Never speed it up with atempo: it sounds chipmunked.
- Long scripts go in 3 chunks split at chapter breaks, passing the previous and next text so the read stays continuous.
- Cut pauses over 0.24 s to 0.16 s, leave 0.5 s at chapter breaks, and add a 0.3 s lead-in.
- Rebuild word times from the alignment into words.js.
- Run faster-whisper over the result and diff it against the script before building the picture.
- Free route: Kokoro, then faster-whisper for the word times.
</voice>

<sound>
- Music: 2-3 free documentary beds from Pixabay, crossfaded over 3 s at big beats.
- Duck the music under the voice (30 ms attack, 0.3 s hold, 0.45 s release) and let it swell back up between chapters.
- SFX from Mixkit, one per event, aligned by their peaks, 6 dB quieter on speech: a typewriter tick on typing, a whoosh on pushes and splats, a pop on tags and cards, a thud on stamps, a hit on every red X, a ding on ticks, plus sounds that fit the scene.
- Gate: during speech the voice sits 15+ dB over music plus SFX (median of 100 ms frames), and the background is louder than the voice in under 1% of frames.
- Two-pass loudnorm to -14 LUFS, true peak -1 dB.
</sound>

<build>
1. Tools: Python, Playwright with Chromium or Edge, FFmpeg, faster-whisper, OpenCV, Pillow, numpy. Install what's missing and tell me what you installed.
2. Order:
   - the look test
   - the art in batches, with a contact sheet after each
   - cutouts and rig
   - voice and word times
   - shots, chapter by chapter
3. Check before any full render: a contact sheet per chapter, one frame every 2 s. Fix:
   - empty or overflowing signs
   - text over a face
   - black plate edges
   - feet floating off the floor
   - two shots in a row in the same place
   - any 4 s where nothing new arrives
4. Render at 30 fps, 4 motion-blur subframes over half a frame, frames piped to libx264 CRF 16-18.
   - Split long videos across 4-6 parallel browser pages and join the parts.
   - Scan the result for single-frame jumps and check that each one is a planned cut.
</build>

<gotchas>
- Too few places reads as lazy. One plate held for 30 s with cards over it looks cheap. Budget about 10 new places a minute.
- Some image models ignore "no arms". GPT Image 2 follows it.
- Paste the same character description into every sheet and feed the base sheet back in, or faces and clothes drift.
- Quad tiles are only about 1920 px wide. Pushing past 1.33x looks soft.
- Plates with people already drawn in can't be animated. Ask for EMPTY and check before cutting.
- Text on a card floating over the art looks like a slideshow. Write on the world.
- Long renders crash. Render in parts you can rerun, and back up the shot files before every big patch.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for my topic, my script, my image model and my voice, then make the look test.
</start>

viral_posts.title_en:
An AI model being fully trained doesn’t mean it stops needing computing power.

Training teaches the model how to recognize patterns, understand language, and generate responses. 

But every time someone uses that model, it still needs computing resources to process the request and produce an answer., This is called inference.

Think about millions of people using ChatGPT simultaneously, generating images, writing code, and running AI agents. Every interaction requires processing power.

Unlike training, inference is an ongoing process. It doesn’t stop when the model is released.

This is why AI companies continue investing billions in data centers and thousands of GPUs.

Building an intelligent model is one challenge. Having enough computing power to serve the world is another.

My Landlord in Dublin Raised My Rent by €600, So I Looked Up Who Owned the Building

I rented a one-bedroom flat in Phib
viral_posts.title_en:
My Landlord in Dublin Raised My Rent by €600, So I Looked Up Who Owned the Building

I rented a one-bedroom flat in Phibsborough, Dublin, for four years. It was old, a bit draughty, and a ten-minute walk from where I worked as a nurse at the Mater Hospital.

My landlord, a man named Declan, lived in Spain and handled everything through a letting agent.

For four years, nothing went wrong.

Then in September, I received an email telling me my rent would increase from €1,450 to €2,050 a month, effective immediately.

I stared at the screen.

I knew enough about Irish tenancy law to understand that rent increases in a Rent Pressure Zone were capped.

Dublin was a Rent Pressure Zone.

I wrote to the agent politely, quoting the rules.

The reply came within an hour.

*This is a new tenancy arrangement. The previous rules do not apply. Please sign the attached agreement within seven days or vacate the property.*

I felt sick.

I was working twelve-hour shifts. I did not have the energy or money to move.

That night, I called my colleague, a ward sister who had been through a similar fight. She told me to contact the Residential Tenancies Board, the RTB, and to check the property registration.

"Landlords have to register every tenancy," she said. "If he hasn't, he's in trouble."

I searched the RTB database.

The flat was registered, but not in Declan's name.

It was registered to a company I had never heard of.

I searched the company name and found something that made my heart race.

The company's director was also listed as the owner of seven other properties on my street.

All of them had received identical rent increases that month.

我在都柏林菲布斯伯勒租了一套一居室公寓，租了四年。它很旧，有点通风，距离我在马特医院当护士的地方有十分钟的步行路程。

我的房东名叫德克兰，住在西班牙，通过租赁代理处理一切事宜。

四年来，没有出过什么差错。

然后在 9 月份，我收到一封电子邮件，告诉我我的租金将从每月 1,450 欧元增加到 2,050 欧元，立即生效。

我盯着屏幕。

我对爱尔兰租赁法有足够的了解，知道租金压力区的租金上涨是有上限的。

都柏林是一个租金压力区。

我礼貌地写信给代理人，引用了规则。

一个小时内就收到了回复。

*这是一项新的租赁安排。以前的规则不适用。请在七天内签署所附协议或腾出该房产。*

我感到恶心。

我十二小时轮班工作。我没有精力或金钱去搬家。

那天晚上，我打电话给我的同事，一位经历过类似斗争的病房姐妹。她让我联系住宅租赁委员会、RTB，并检查财产登记。

“房东必须登记每一份租约，”她说。 “如果他不这么做，他就有麻烦了。”

我搜索了 RTB 数据库。

这套公寓已登记，但不是以德克兰的名义。

它注册于一家我从未听说过的公司。

我搜索了公司名称，发现了一些让我心跳加速的东西。

该公司的董事还被列为我所在街道上另外七处房产的所有者。

当月他们所有人都获得了相同的租金上涨。

AI agents hiring other AI agents to create something? that's getting interesting. 

@termix_ai recently introduced Monta
viral_posts.title_en:
AI agents hiring other AI agents to create something? that's getting interesting. 

@termix_ai recently introduced Montage Studio, an AI agent that can turn a simple brief into a complete music video or advertisement.

What caught my attention is that it doesn't do everything alone.

It hires three specialized agents for storyboarding, video rendering and music production, then combines their work into a finished 1080p video.

There's also a campaign attached:

→ Minimum qualifying order: 31.5 USDC
→ Reward: 15,750 TermiX Points
→ One qualifying purchase per wallet
→ X account linking required 

Just to be clear, 31.5 USDC is the minimum campaign requirement, not a fixed service price.
But the bigger thing I'm interested in is the technology behind it.

TermiX's AACP is designed to let agents discover each other, hire services, manage payments through escrow, verify delivery and settle transactions.

In simple terms, one agent can find a job, hire other agents to complete different parts of it, and bring everything together.

Montage Studio is a pretty practical example of what an agent economy could actually look like.

Not just agents answering prompts, but agents working together and creating something people are willing to pay for.

explore here: https://t.co/ISFSBXCim6

@termix_ai 最近推出了 Montage Studio，这是一种人工智能代理，可以将简单的简介变成完整的音乐视频或广告。

引起我注意的是它并不能单独完成所有事情。

它聘请了三名专门的代理来制作故事板、视频渲染和音乐制作，然后将他们的工作组合成最终的 1080p 视频。

还附带了一个活动：

→ 最低合格订单：31.5 USDC
→ 奖励：15,750 TermiX 积分
→ 每个钱包一次合格购买
→ 需要 X 帐户链接

需要明确的是，31.5 USDC 是活动的最低要求，而不是固定的服务价格。
但我更感兴趣的是其背后的技术。

TermiX 的 AACP 旨在让代理商相互发现、租赁服务、通过托管管理付款、验证交付和结算交易。

简而言之，一个代理人可以找到一份工作，雇用其他代理人来完成工作的不同部分，然后将所有内容整合在一起。

Montage Studio 是代理经济的一个非常实际的例子。

不仅仅是代理回答提示，而是代理一起工作并创造人们愿意付费的东西。
